transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: A solution contains \(25\)% acid and the rest water. If \(40\) litres of water are added to \(60\) litres of this solution, what is the percentage of acid in the new mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Acid in 60 L = \(0.25\times60 = 15\) L
Water added = 40 L ⇒ total mixture = 100 L
Acid % = \(\tfrac{15}{100}\times100 = 15\)%

questions.stem: In what ratio should water be mixed with milk costing Rs. \(18\) per litre so that the mixture is worth Rs. \(16\) per litre?
questions.keySolution: By alligation: \((18-16):(16-0)=2:16=1:8\). Hence water : milk = \(1:8\).

questions.stem: A mixture of \(120\) litres contains milk and water in the ratio \(3:2\). How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio \(1:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Milk = \(\frac{3}{5}\times120 = 72\) L
Water = \(48\) L
Let \(x\) L water be added: \(\frac{72}{48+x}=1\Rightarrow x=24\) L

questions.stem: A \(40\)-litre solution contains \(20\)% alcohol. How many litres of pure alcohol must be added so that alcohol becomes \(50\)% of the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Alcohol = \(0.20\times40 = 8\) L
Let \(x\) L alcohol be added: \(\tfrac{8+x}{40+x}=0.5\Rightarrow x=24\) L

questions.stem: Vessel A contains \(60\)% milk and vessel B contains \(40\)% milk. In what ratio should they be mixed to obtain a mixture with \(50\)% milk?
questions.keySolution: Alligation gives equal differences (10 each) ⇒ ratio \(1:1\).

questions.stem: An 80-kg solution contains \(30\)% salt. If \(20\) kg of pure salt is added, what is the percentage of salt in the resulting mixture?
questions.keySolution: Salt = \(0.30\times80 = 24\) kg → add 20 kg ⇒ 44 kg in 100 kg ⇒ \(44\)%.

questions.stem: A 50-litre mixture contains \(40\)% acid. Ten litres are withdrawn and replaced with water. Find the percentage of acid in the new mixture.
questions.keySolution:
Acid removed = \(0.4\times10 = 4\) L
Acid left = 20 − 4 = 16 L in 50 L ⇒ \(32\)%.

questions.stem: Sixty litres of a mixture of alcohol and water are in the ratio \(2:1\). How many litres of alcohol must be added so that the ratio becomes \(3:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Alcohol = 40 L, water = 20 L.
Let \(x\) L alcohol be added: \(\tfrac{40+x}{20}=\tfrac{3}{1}\Rightarrow x=20\) L.

questions.stem: A 100-litre mixture has oil and water in the ratio \(3:7\). How many litres of oil should be added so that the final ratio becomes \(1:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Oil = 30 L, water = 70 L.
Let \(x\) L oil be added: \(30+x=70\Rightarrow x=40\) L.

questions.stem: A mixture contains \(25\)% copper and \(75\)% zinc. If \(12\) kg of zinc is added to \(48\) kg of this mixture, what is the percentage of copper in the new mixture?
questions.keySolution: Copper = \(0.25\times48=12\) kg; total mass = 60 kg ⇒ \(\tfrac{12}{60}\times100=20\)%.

questions.stem: A vessel holds \(120\) litres of pure milk. Twenty litres are replaced with water twice. What is the final milk : water ratio?
questions.keySolution:
Fraction milk after one replacement = \(\tfrac{100}{120}=\tfrac{5}{6}\).
After two: \((\tfrac{5}{6})^{2}=\tfrac{25}{36}\).
Milk = \(\tfrac{25}{36}\times120=\tfrac{250}{3}\) L;
water = \(120-\tfrac{250}{3}=\tfrac{110}{3}\) L ⇒ ratio 25 : 11.

questions.stem: Two alloys contain gold and silver in ratios \(5:3\) and \(3:5\). How many kilograms of each are needed to make \(40\) kg of alloy with equal gold and silver?
questions.keySolution:
Gold%: alloy1 = 62.5, alloy2 = 37.5, target = 50.
Alligation ⇒ ratio 1:1 ⇒ 20 kg each.

questions.stem: An 80-litre mixture contains \(25\)% alcohol. How many litres of water must evaporate so that alcohol becomes \(40\)% of the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Alcohol = 20 L (constant).
Let \(x\) L water evaporate ⇒ mixture = 80 − x.
\(\tfrac{20}{80-x}=0.4\Rightarrow x=30\) L.

questions.stem: Twenty litres of a mixture (\(45\)% acid) are replaced by water, and the acid percentage falls to \(36\)%. Find the original volume of the mixture.
questions.keySolution:
Let volume = \(x\) L; acid = 0.45x.
Acid removed = 0.45×20 = 9 L.
Remaining acid = 0.45x − 9 = 0.36x ⇒ x = 100 L.

questions.stem: Tea costing Rs. \(126\) kg and Rs. \(135\) kg are mixed with a tea costing Rs. \(175.50\) kg. If the mixture costs Rs. \(153\) kg, find the ratio of the three varieties.
questions.keySolution: Using weighted-average equation yields smallest integers 3 : 1 : 2.

questions.stem: Fifty litres of a solution contain \(30\)% alcohol. Ten litres of water are removed. What is the alcohol percentage now?
questions.keySolution: Alcohol = 15 L (unchanged); volume = 40 L ⇒ \(\tfrac{15}{40}\times100=37.5\)%.

questions.stem: A 45-litre solution has \(20\)% alcohol. How much pure alcohol must be added so that alcohol becomes \(35\)% of the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Alcohol = 9 L.
Let \(x\) L be added: \(\tfrac{9+x}{45+x}=0.35\Rightarrow x=10.38\) L.

questions.stem: Solutions with \(25\)% and \(40\)% acid are mixed in the ratio \(3:2\). Find the acid percentage in the mixture.
questions.keySolution: Weighted mean = \(\tfrac{3\times25+2\times40}{5}=31\)%.

questions.stem: Coffee at Rs. \(60\) kg is mixed with coffee at Rs. \(65\) kg to get a blend worth Rs. \(63.20\) kg. What is the mixing ratio?
A tank holds \(120\) litres of a mix containing \(25\)% kerosene. How much kerosene must be added so that kerosene becomes \(40\)% of the mixture?
questions.keySolution:
Kerosene = 30 L.
Let \(x\) L be added: \(\tfrac{30+x}{120+x}=0.4\Rightarrow x=30\) L.

questions.stem: Twenty litres of \(35\)% alcohol solution are mixed with \(30\) litres of \(20\)% solution. What is the alcohol percentage of the mixture?
A cask is \(\tfrac{1}{5}\) emptied and refilled with water twice. What fraction of the final mixture is original wine?
questions.keySolution:
Fraction remaining after each replacement = \((1-\tfrac{1}{5})=\tfrac{4}{5}\).
After two ⇒ \((\tfrac{4}{5})^{2}=\tfrac{16}{25}\).

questions.stem: Forty kilograms of a mix with milk : water = \(3:1\). How much water should be added so that the ratio becomes \(2:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Milk = 30 kg, water = 10 kg.
Let \(x\) kg water be added: \(\tfrac{30}{10+x}=\tfrac{2}{1}\Rightarrow x=5\) kg.

questions.stem: A 40-g mix contains \(40\)% gold. If \(15\) g gold is added, what is the new gold percentage?
Ninety litres of solution are \(40\)% acid. How many litres of acid must be added to make it \(50\)% acid?
questions.keySolution:
Acid = 36 L.
Let \(x\) L be added: \(\tfrac{36+x}{90+x}=0.5\Rightarrow x=18\) L.

questions.stem: To prepare \(300\) L of \(30\)% chemical, how much of \(25\)% and \(40\)% solutions are needed?
questions.keySolution:
Alligation ⇒ ratio \(2:1\) (25% : 40%).
Hence 200 L of 25% and 100 L of 40%.

questions.stem: Sixty litres of \(12\)% boric acid solution are diluted to \(8\)% by adding water. How much water is added?
questions.keySolution:
Acid = 7.2 L.
Let volume after addition = 60 + x.
\(\tfrac{7.2}{60+x}=0.08\Rightarrow x=30\) L.

questions.stem: A vessel has \(20\) L of \(25\)% acid. How much \(75\)% acid should be added to obtain \(50\)% acid solution?
questions.keySolution:
Acid = 5 L + 0.75x.
Total = 20 + x.
\(\tfrac{5+0.75x}{20+x}=0.5\Rightarrow x=20\) L.

questions.stem: A 75-litre mixture has milk : water = \(2:1\). How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio \(1:1\)?
questions.keySolution:
Milk = 50 L, water = 25 L.
Need water so that water = milk ⇒ add 25 L.

questions.stem: A 50-kg mix is \(20\)% sand. How much sand must be added to make sand \(25\)% of the mix?
questions.keySolution:
Sand = 10 kg.
Let \(x\) kg be added: \(\tfrac{10+x}{50+x}=0.25\Rightarrow x=\tfrac{10}{3}\) kg.

questions.stem: A solution contains \(60\)% alcohol. If \(30\) litres of water are added to \(60\) litres of this solution, what is the alcohol percentage now?
questions.keySolution: Alcohol = 36 L (unchanged); total = 90 L ⇒ \(40\)%.
